title: Hidden Piston Door
lead: Flip a lever, and a wall of bookshelves slides apart. Hide it in a bookcase, and it is hard to spot.

states.label: Closed
states.text: The lever is off. The Redstone Torch is on, so all 4 Sticky Pistons push. The bookshelves fill the doorway.

states.label: Open
states.text: You flip the lever on. The torch goes out, and the pistons pull the bookshelves into the wall. Walk right through!

steps: Stack 2 Sticky Pistons with their sticky faces pointing right. Leave a gap 4 blocks wide. Then stack 2 more facing left.
Put a Bookshelf against the sticky face of each piston. These 4 bookshelves are your door.
Behind each piston stack, on the side away from your base, place a block. Put Redstone Dust on top.
Join the two sides with a bridge of blocks behind the doorway. Step up, go over the top, then step down.
Put Redstone Dust on top of every bridge block.
To the right of the right pistons, place a block, and one more behind it. Put dust on both.
Place one more block to the right, with a Redstone Torch on top. The door slides shut.
Put a Lever on the front of the torch's block. Flip it to open the door!
how: A Redstone Torch stays on until the block under it gets power. While the lever is off, the torch powers the dust. The dust powers all 4 Sticky Pistons, and they push the bookshelves together. Flip the lever on, and it powers the torch's block. The torch turns off, so the pistons pull the bookshelves back.
tips: A normal Piston can push the door shut, but it cannot pull it open again.
In Bedrock, Redstone Dust turns to point at a piston's back or side by itself. The dust powers the top piston, and the block under the dust powers the bottom one.
Do not let the lever's block touch a piston. A piston turns on when a block next to it has power.
Build a wall of Bookshelves on the outside, in front of the redstone. Leave the 2 by 2 doorway open.
Put a Slimeball on top of a Piston in the crafting grid.
